chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd al-Yaqṭīnī wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who handed over his son to another man for a year with a known wage so that he might sew for him; then another man came and said to him, "Hand over your son to me for a year for an increased wage." Does he have the choice in that, and is it permissible for him to revoke what he had agreed upon with the first one, or not?
So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: "He must fulfill the agreement with the first one so long as illness or weakness does not occur to his son."

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: the option or choice to proceed or withdraw
key_terms.ضَعْفٌ: weakness that prevents continuing the work
key_terms.لِيَخِيطَ: to sew; to perform tailoring work
key_terms.يَفْسَخَ: to revoke or cancel an agreement

ai.seo_question: Can a prior wage agreement be canceled if a better employment offer appears later?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on honoring an existing labor agreement involving a son's service for a fixed wage and term. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the first agreement must be fulfilled and cannot be revoked merely for a better offer, unless the son becomes ill or weak.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3654 - Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid Al-Yaqtini wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali bin Muhammad Al-Askari (as), asking:

"A man entrusted his son to another man and handed him over for a year with a known wage to sew for him. Then another man came and said to him, 'Hand over your son to me for a year with an increased wage.'
Does he have the choice in this matter, and is it permissible for him to revoke the agreement made with the first man or not?"
Imam (as) replied in his handwriting: 'He must fulfill the agreement with the first man unless his son faces illness or weakness.'
